text:
maya: FYI nightly evals just flagged a big quality flip for the q8 quantized build on the "redwood-small" family. F1 down ~6-8% on several prompt suites, but only when prefix caching enabled :thinking:

sam: hmm, any repro? is it happening across seeds or only specific prompts? :eyes:

maya: repro is fairly consistent. quick summary: nightly-run shows 24->128 failures for our customer-facing prompt set bank. locally i can reproduce with two different completion calls that share the same 64-char start of system+user prefix but diverge after — outputs are identical (looks like a cache hit).

alex: that smells like cache key truncation. we recently switched to a 64-char prefix key to speed index lookups for large prompts.

jena: can you paste the exact key code?

maya: snippet from serving runtime config:

```python
# simplified
def make_prefix_key(model, quant, prompt):
    return f"{model}:{quant}:{prompt[:64]}"
```

maya: so any two prompts that share the first 64 chars collide. with batching and async kv writes this becomes nondeterministic across requests.

sam: confirmed locally: i ran two calls with identical first 64 chars and different suffixes. first call produced A, second call also returned A even though they diverged later. reproducible with curl: 

```bash
curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-q8","prompt":"PREFIX-IDENTICAL-.......<suffix-1>","max_tokens":40}'

curl -s -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_KEY" \
  -d '{"model":"redwood-small-q8","prompt":"PREFIX-IDENTICAL-.......<suffix-2>","max_tokens":40}'
```

sam: both returned same generation payload and logs show a cache_hit for key `redwood-small-q8:q8:PREFIX-IDENTICAL-.......`

alex: oh wow. and this only shows up on q8 build?

maya: we see it much worse on q8 and q4_0 quant builds. float32 baseline rarely shows it because cache is disabled in that path for now. quantized runtime shares the prefix cache helper (fast path) which uses the truncated key.

jena: impact scope: nightly eval -> model onboarding failures; customer traffic -> incorrect completions for multi-tenant prompts with similar system messages. This could silently degrade quality.

infra-bot: CI job nightly-evals/1790 reported 104 regressions for redwood-small-q8 at 2026-03-05T02:11:46Z

eva: suggested quick mitigation: namespace cache keys by full prompt hash and model+quant tag. E.g. key = f"{model}:{quant}:sha256(prefix+rest)" or at minimum include prompt length byte to reduce prefix collisions.

alex: agree. low-risk hotfix: switch key from truncated prefix to first-64 + total_length + model+quant hash. that keeps index perf but reduces collisions while we evaluate full-hash cost.

sam: i can whip up a patch. plan:
- push hotfix to staging runtime to compute key as: `{model}:{quant}:{prefix[:64]}:{len(prefix)}`
- run nightly eval subset to confirm drop in regressions
- if stable, roll to canary for customer beta tier

maya: also flagging we should add a regression test in nightly-evals harness that creates two different prompts with same first-64 and asserts outputs differ (unless intentionally cached).

jena: good call. please add a test case and a short note in the model-onboarding checklist about cache-key hygiene for quant paths.

sam: pushed draft PR with runtime change and unit test: https://git.internal/redwood/runtime/pulls/568 :eyes: (still draft, needs review)

maya: ran quick staging job - metrics look promising: reduced the failing prompts from 128 -> 6 in the sampled set. putting a follow-up run to cover more prompt banks overnight.

eva: longer term: we should move to stable sha256 of full prompt for correctness and measure perf delta. but short-term length+prefix fix is fine. also audit any other places that use truncated prompt keys (prewarm, prefetch, dedupe).

alex: can we add a trace flag to log raw keys for a minute in prod canary to be sure we don't miss other collision shapes? only for canary customers.

maya: yes i'll add a per-deployment env var TRACE_PREFIX_KEYS=true to log hashed_key and truncated_key to structured logs for 1 hour during canary.

jena: ok timeline: sam -> hotfix PR today, maya -> staging run tonight, canary rollout tomorrow AM if green. i'll own documentation and nightly test update.

sam: thanks all. tagging ops for awareness: @infra (adding to rotation)

infra-bot: deploy scheduled: runtime/canary -> 10% at 2026-03-06T09:00:00Z (pending manual approve)

maya: high priority but low blast - feels like a good quick win. filing a short postmortem template after canary results.

alex: +1. cc:eng-runtime for follow-up perf measurement on sha256 option.

jena: cool. i'll drop a summary in the onboarding doc and close the loop after canary. :white_check_mark:
